clusters.name: Teodor's death, 1978–1979
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Teodor's death in January 1978, within the following months: your grandmother Delphine stopped cooking and went to your mother's every evening; your father took night shifts and kept his distance from your mother; your uncle Anton drank at lunch and separated from Celeste; your mother lay awake over them; and your brother Callum had ear infections all winter. By May 1979, your grandmother took a job at the library and was out of the house every day, and the shifts settled.

clusters.name: Odette's bed rest, 1984–1985
clusters.reason: Around your mother's bed rest in March 1984, within the following months: your grandmother Hazel came every morning to keep the house; your father argued with her over how she kept it; your brother Callum stammered again; and you could not sleep unless your father sat by the bed. By September 1984, your sister Ines was born, and the household settled into a new pattern.

clusters.name: Hazel's Parkinson's diagnosis, 1986–1997
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's diagnosis in September 1986, within the following years: your grandfather Ambrose took over her cooking and appointments; your father phoned his father every night for news of her and later argued with Uncle Lyle over who should help; your grandfather had chest pains; Hazel fell and walked with a frame, then could no longer dress herself or stand; your mother took her to the clinic twice a week; your aunt Mavis came to stay one week in four to nurse her; your father drank most evenings; your aunt Pearl had panic spells at the wheel. In June 1997, Hazel moved to the Fairlie nursing home, and by October your father cut his drinking back to weekends.

clusters.name: Callum leaving home, 1999–2000
clusters.reason: Around your brother Callum leaving for a job up north in May 1999, within the preceding and following months: your father and he argued most nights over his plans; your mother could not settle at the thought of him so far away; your father missed days at work and sat up late in the garage; your sister Ines skipped school most of that autumn; your mother took Ines with her everywhere; and by August 2000, Ines was back at school full days and passed her exams.

clusters.name: Hazel's death, 2003
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Hazel's death in January 2003, within the following months: you could not sleep more than a few hours a night; you stopped going in to the bookshop and were let go in May; you dreaded buses and crowded shops and went out only after dark. By November 2003, you took a job at the garden centre and were sleeping through the night again, and the shifts settled.
